headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from MCP-enabled OpenMetadata interacting with Caveman’s file/LLM workflows; no direct evidence of a shared channel, so uncertainty is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP, APIs, events, and webhooks, while Caveman uses MCP and reads/writes files like CLAUDE.md and project notes. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if OpenMetadata content is surfaced into Caveman’s trusted context. No direct pairwise evidence is provided, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata content is routed into Caveman prompts or files without provenance tagging
IF Caveman treats file contents or MCP payloads as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata text into Caveman prompts
Require provenance labels on all MCP/webhook payloads before display
Restrict Caveman to read-only access to shared notes
Add a manual review step before any instruction-like content is executed
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents onto separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge through APIs and MCP. If they share a workspace or metadata channel, sensitive operational context can flow between them. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this remains medium, not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or metadata store
IF Caveman exports session logs or memory files into OpenMetadata-managed records
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Remove sensitive notes from shared directories
Turn off automatic file syncing into OpenMetadata
Review and redact session logs before import
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and OpenMetadata can act through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP while Caveman operates on files and LLM tool use. Overlapping writes to shared metadata or notes could race or overwrite each other. No locking or shared-resource coordination is documented, so the conflict is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same notes, metadata, or configuration files
IF no external lock or transaction layer is configured
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate write directory
Use file locks or a single-writer policy
Schedule writes in non-overlapping windows
Audit for conflicting updates after each run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman can generate or edit project notes and CLAUDE.md, and OpenMetadata can propagate metadata through APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If OpenMetadata consumes Caveman output as authoritative, a mistaken note can cascade into catalog or governance actions. Because the downstream blast radius can affect multiple work products and compliance-relevant metadata, high is warranted.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Caveman-produced notes or instructions without verification
IF downstream workflows auto-publish metadata or governance changes from that input
mitigations: Require human approval before publishing metadata changes
Add validation against source-of-truth systems
Mark Caveman output as untrusted by default
Limit OpenMetadata to draft-only ingestion from Caveman
requires-engineering: implement provenance and rollback for propagated changes

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge, while Caveman handles session logs and project notes. If those notes contain regulated or residency-sensitive data, differing retention or residency policies could create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Caveman notes or session logs
IF OpenMetadata retention or residency settings differ from the source system
mitigations: Classify data before syncing it into OpenMetadata
Exclude regulated fields from project notes
Document retention rules for both systems
Review residency settings before enabling sync
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both platforms
